metadata.title: How to promote intrinsically versus extrinsically motivated teachers’ job satisfaction: Exploring individual and school factors

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses the Korean Educational Longitudinal Study (KELS) 2013 teacher questionnaire, with schools selected via stratified cluster random sampling (242 elementary schools). The manuscript does not report any student-level sampling/survey weight variables or replicate-weight procedures, and the analyses are conducted with SPSS sequential linear regression and Mplus multigroup CFA/SEM using the “type is complex” command to account for clustering of teachers within schools. Because no explicit weight variable names (e.g., TOTWGT/W_FSTUWT) are provided, it is unclear whether complex-sample weights were applied beyond the clustering-robust specification. For replication, analysts should use the KELS-provided complex-sample design variables if available; otherwise, they should at minimum apply clustering-robust estimation at the school level as done here.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: The dependent variable is teachers’ job satisfaction measured via Likert-scale survey items and modeled with regression and multigroup CFA/SEM; there are no plausible values (PV) generated for cognitive achievement domains in this dataset. Missing data are handled using full information maximum likelihood (FIML), which is a model-based approach that uses all available information under the missing-at-random assumption; however, the paper does not describe any PV-based missingness workflow because PVs are not part of this measurement framework.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Data come from KELS 2013 teacher questionnaire, using the first two waves because the survey was administered to teachers only during those years. The analytic sample includes 3677 teachers from 242 elementary schools selected through stratified cluster random sampling. Teachers were excluded if they did not indicate their primary job selection motives (n=19) or if they constructed their own responses via the open-ended option (n=121), leaving two groups based on primary motive: extrinsically motivated (nEXT=1655) and intrinsically motivated (nINT=1882).

main_findings.performance_metrics: Sequential linear regression (Table 4): Model 1 R2=0.009; Model 2 R2=0.177 (ΔR2=0.169, p<.001); Model 3 R2=0.244 (ΔR2=0.068, p<.001). Final-step standardized betas: non-tenure β=0.09; years experience β=-0.09; self-efficacy teaching β=0.14; self-efficacy classroom management β=0.20; colleague passion β=0.19; collaboration β=0.06; conflicts β=-0.05; principal support β=0.06.
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using KELS 2013 teacher questionnaire data from 242 Korean elementary schools (2013–2014 waves), the study leveraged non-tenure status, years of teaching experience, self-efficacy in teaching, self-efficacy in classroom management, and colleague teachers’ passion to predict teachers’ job satisfaction, finding that classroom-management self-efficacy and colleague passion were positive predictors while years of experience and colleague conflicts were negative predictors. This indicates that teacher professional development and school-level morale-building should prioritize classroom management capability and collegial enthusiasm to sustain job satisfaction, especially as experience increases.

main_findings.dataset_used: KELS 2013 (teacher questionnaire), multigroup SEM (extrinsically vs intrinsically motivated teachers)
main_findings.target_variable: Teachers’ job satisfaction (moderated by job selection motive)
main_findings.performance_metrics: Multigroup SEM (Table 6 fit indices): baseline CFA full sample n=3530 RMSEA=0.046, CFI=0.941; multigroup SEM RMSEA=0.049, CFI=0.920. Significant group-differential paths (RQ2): non-tenure significant only for extrinsically motivated (βEXT=0.07, p<.001); years experience negative for both (βEXT=-0.05, p<.05; βINT=-0.14, p<.001) with stronger effect for intrinsically motivated (Δχ2(1)=6.375, p=.012). Self-efficacy teaching significant only for intrinsically motivated (βINT=0.13, p<.05). Classroom-management self-efficacy significant for both (βEXT=0.23, p<.001; βINT=0.25, p<.001). Colleague passion significant for both (βEXT=0.30, p<.001; βINT=0.17, p<.001) with significant deterioration when constrained (Δχ2(1)=5.783, p=.016).
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using KELS 2013 teacher questionnaire data and multigroup SEM comparing extrinsically versus intrinsically motivated teachers, the study leveraged non-tenure status, years of teaching experience, self-efficacy in teaching, self-efficacy in classroom management, and colleague teachers’ passion to predict job satisfaction, finding that classroom-management self-efficacy was a consistent positive predictor across both groups while colleague passion was the only significant school-climate predictor and was more salient for extrinsically motivated teachers. This indicates that differentiated retention and well-being strategies should combine universal classroom-management support with group-tailored school climate interventions that strengthen collegial morale, rather than relying on collaboration or principal support alone.

data.outcome_summary: The study analyzes KELS 2013 teacher questionnaire data from 242 Korean elementary schools (3677 teachers; extrinsically motivated n=1655, intrinsically motivated n=1882) using sequential linear regression and multigroup CFA/SEM in Mplus with clustering accounted for at the school level. In the sequential regression, the final model explained R²=0.244 of job satisfaction variance, with self-efficacy in classroom management (β=0.20) and colleague teachers’ passion (β=0.19) as positive predictors, while years of teaching experience (β=-0.09) and conflicts with colleagues (β=-0.05) were negative. In multigroup SEM, model fit was acceptable (multigroup SEM CFI=0.920, RMSEA=0.049), and classroom-management self-efficacy predicted job satisfaction for both groups (βEXT=0.23; βINT=0.25). Self-efficacy in teaching mattered only for intrinsically motivated teachers, and colleague passion was the sole significant school-level predictor, stronger for extrinsically motivated teachers (βEXT=0.30 vs βINT=0.17). Limitations include cross-sectional design (no causal inference) and no explicit reporting of PVs or survey weights beyond complex-sample clustering handling.
